answer: Seed-anchored trust propagation resists sybils: influence equals trust mass that random-walks out from a hand-verified honest core, attenuating at every hop, with restarts teleporting only back to the seed. A gale of internal cross-links inside a sybil reef just recirculates mass among fakes — it cannot manufacture new flow across the few genuine edges entering the cluster. A distant nebula of fakes receives vanishing mass however densely it interlinks; honest nodes near the seed hold high score. Total sybil influence is bounded by real trust crossing into the region, not by their edge count.
